title: Impact of Control-Packet Loss on the Delay of Active Reliable Multicast in Lossy Wireless Mesh Backhauls: An M/G/1 Model Validated by Discrete-Event Simulation
content: Wireless mesh networks offer a cost-effective multi-hop backhaul, but unreliable links, limited bandwidth and growing networks can degrade multicast performance. We analyse the delay of two active reliable multicast protocols, AMRHy (hybrid) and DyRAM (receiver-initiated). In our M/G/1 model, every node serves data packets, ACKs and NACKs, control packets are lost and retransmitted hop by hop, NACKs are repeated with an exponential back-off and NACKs triggered by an upstream loss reach the tail relay in bursts. The evaluation varies loss probability, backbone depth, group size and packet rate. A packet-level discrete-event simulation of the same mechanisms, with idealised replier election and ACK suppression validates the model within 9% inside its validity domain (27 configurations per protocol). At the reference rate of 0.05 packets/ms, AMRHy repairs a lost packet in 19.5 ms against 44.9 ms for DyRAM, whose receivers detect a loss only when the next packet arrives. The delay ratio falls from 7.4 at 0.01 packets/ms to 1.6 at 0.1 packet/ms. Losing control packets as often as data packets increases the delay by at most 10% and NACK bursts limit both protocols beyond 54 to 56 receivers per group. These results support hybrid loss recovery, especially for low-rate sessions.
